meta.routeLine: Rome (3) → Naples (2) → Amalfi (2) → Florence (3) → Tuscany (2) → Rome finale (1)

meta.chainStory: Hotel Trame (Rome, independent) → Grand Hotel Vesuvio (Naples, Leading Hotels of the World) → Anantara Convento (Amalfi, Minor / GHA) → The Hoxton Florence (independent) → Il Castelfalfi (Tuscany, TUI Blue Selection) → Nobu Hotel Roma (Rome, Nobu Hospitality)

days.title: Landing in Rome
days.kicker: ROME — Hotel Trame, by the Pantheon
days.note: Jet-lag day. Nothing ticketed, nothing timed — the only fixed point is dinner.

items.title: Land at FCO
items.detail: Immigration + bags, about 45 min

items.title: Private driver to Hotel Trame
items.detail: Pre-booked NCC, meeting you inside arrivals with a name board. Licensed cars may enter the ZTL to set down, so you are dropped at the hotel door — no garage, no walk with the bags.

items.title: Check in at Hotel Trame
items.detail: A former Franciscan monastery a few streets off Campo de' Fiori

items.title: First walk: Pantheon → Piazza Navona → Campo de' Fiori
items.detail: The Pantheon is an eight-minute walk. Go before the nap, not after.

items.title: Nap, deliberately
items.detail: Set an alarm. This is the single best defence against day-two jet lag.

items.title: Aperitivo at Etabli
items.detail: Or the Campari bar on Campo de' Fiori

items.title: Dinner — Armando al Pantheon
items.detail: Tiny, family-run, and booked out weeks ahead. Reserve now.

days.title: The Vatican, before anyone else
days.note: Early entry is the whole point: the Sistine Chapel is a different room with 40 people in it than with 400.

items.title: Vatican early-entry private tour
items.detail: Into the Sistine Chapel before general admission

items.title: Lunch — Da Romolo or Hostaria Dino e Tony
items.detail: Unfussy Roman cooking a short walk from the museum exit

items.title: Back to the hotel through the heat
items.detail: Late August in Rome peaks around 3pm. Don't fight it.

items.title: Castel Sant'Angelo, then the bridge at sunset
items.detail: Ponte Sant'Angelo with Bernini's angels catching the last light

items.title: Rooftop aperitivo near Campo de' Fiori
OPERA — arias at All Saints' Anglican Church
items.detail: Confirm the Aug 25 programme; Via del Babuino, off Piazza di Spagna

items.title: Late dinner — Pierluigi
items.detail: Seafood on Piazza de' Ricci; a properly Roman hour to eat

days.title: Ancient Rome, end to end
days.note: Last Roman day before the south — this afternoon is also the Villa Borghese photo session, so the siesta runs shorter than usual.

items.title: Colosseum with arena floor, then Forum + Palatine
items.detail: The arena-floor add-on is worth it — you stand where the sand was

items.title: Lunch — Roscioli
items.detail: Carbonara and cacio e pepe, and the deli counter on the way out
items.how: Walk, 5 min via Campo de' Fiori

items.title: Siesta
items.detail: Shorter than the other days — the light at Borghese is worth trading a bit of rest for

items.title: Villa Borghese Gardens, in the daylight
items.detail: Rome's largest park — shaded avenues, the Fontana dei Cavalli Marini, and the Pincio terrace over Piazza del Popolo with St. Peter's dome on the skyline. Soft light under the trees most of the afternoon — good ground for pictures. The Galleria itself needs a timed ticket booked weeks out; skip it unless you already have one.

items.title: Down to Piazza del Popolo
items.detail: The twin churches and the obelisk, down the Pincio steps

items.title: Trastevere on foot
items.detail: Cross the Tiber and wander to Piazza Santa Maria in Trastevere

items.title: Dinner — Da Enzo al 29
items.detail: Trastevere, twelve tables, no reservations after 9pm

days.title: South to Naples, by rail
days.changeNote: Naples now follows Rome directly rather than Florence — the confirmed Grand Hotel Vesuvio booking sits on Via Partenope, an easy Frecciarossa hop south.

items.title: Check out; taxi to Roma Termini
items.detail: About fifteen minutes from Campo de' Fiori

items.title: Frecciarossa to Naples
items.detail: Roma Termini → Napoli Centrale, direct — about 1h10. Trains run roughly every half hour; no need to book far ahead.

items.title: Drop bags — Grand Hotel Vesuvio
items.detail: Via Partenope, facing Castel dell'Ovo and the bay. Rooms are ready from 3:00pm; they will hold luggage until then.

items.title: Spaccanapoli and the old city
items.detail: The dead-straight Greek road that still splits Naples in half — pizza fritta and sfogliatelle along the way

items.title: Aperitivo — Sky Lounge
items.detail: The hotel's rooftop bar, one floor below dinner

items.title: Dinner — Caruso Roof Garden
items.detail: Ninth floor, Michelin-starred, named for Enrico Caruso, who called this hotel his Neapolitan home. Reservations open only 14 days out — call as soon as the window opens. The Bucatini alla Caruso is the dish to order.

days.title: Capri, by ferry
days.note: Weather-dependent. The Blue Grotto only opens in a flat sea — treat it as a bonus, not a plan. Buy the return leg when you buy the outbound, and check the last sailing before you settle in for the afternoon.

items.title: Walk down to Molo Beverello
items.detail: The fast-ferry pier is fifteen minutes along the seafront from the hotel

items.title: Fast ferry — Naples → Capri
items.detail: NLG, SNAV and Caremar all run it in about fifty minutes. Sailings are frequent in summer but sell out at the counter — book online the night before.

items.title: The Faraglioni, the grottoes, the swim coves
items.detail: Pick up a round-the-island boat at Marina Grande — Blue Grotto if the sea is calm enough to enter

items.title: Lunch — Da Paolino
items.detail: Under the lemon trees. Il Riccio is the Michelin alternative, on the cliff by the grotto.

items.title: The Piazzetta and the Gardens of Augustus
items.detail: Gelato on the terrace above Via Krupp

items.title: Ferry back to Naples
items.detail: Check the final sailing when you arrive — the last fast boats go early evening, and missing one means a night on the island

items.title: Dinner — Palazzo Petrucci
items.detail: Michelin-starred Neapolitan tasting menu, back in the old city — the celebration dinner for the boat day

days.title: Down the coast by sea, via Positano
days.changeNote: Replaces a private-driver transfer — a seasonal Naples–Positano–Amalfi ferry runs July–August, and it's a far better way to see the coast for the first time than through a windshield.
days.note: Positano has no real port, just a pier that closes in rough seas — check the operator's morning update if the forecast looks unsettled. The route only runs July–August, so it won't be there outside this window.

items.title: Walk to Molo Beverello
items.detail: Fifteen minutes along the seafront

items.title: Ferry to Positano and Amalfi
items.detail: Positano Jet and a couple of other operators run this seasonal route — book the Amalfi-bound leg specifically, not just the Positano hop.

items.title: Positano from the water
items.detail: The pastel stairs climbing straight up from the sea — the best view of the town is from the boat, not the beach

items.title: Arrive Amalfi marina; lunch nearby
items.detail: A table just off Piazza Duomo before checking in

items.title: Amalfi's Duomo and the old town
items.detail: The striped façade of Sant'Andrea and the Cloister of Paradise, then the lemon-lined lanes behind the piazza

items.title: Check in — Anantara Convento di Amalfi
items.detail: Deluxe Sea View Room. A 13th-century monastery on the cliff edge, with the original cloister still standing.

items.title: Dinner — Dei Cappuccini
items.detail: The hotel's Michelin room, or La Locanda for pizza if the day has beaten you

days.title: Ravello, above everything
days.note: The Ravello Festival runs to Sep 5, well past tonight — check what's actually on. The switchbacks up from the coast are tight and slow, and there's no rental car this stretch, so a private driver handles this leg.

items.title: The beach club, by cliff lift
items.detail: A slow morning at sea level before the day starts properly

items.title: Lunch — Lo Scoglio
items.detail: Nerano. The original spaghetti alla Nerano, and worth the boat ride on its own.

items.title: Up to Ravello
items.detail: Forty-five minutes of switchbacks above the coast

items.title: Villa Cimbrone
items.detail: The Terrace of Infinity — a marble balustrade lined with busts, and a thousand-foot drop to the sea

items.title: RAVELLO FESTIVAL — check the Aug 30 programme
items.detail: Confirmed concerts run to Sep 5 — check what's actually on tonight before you commit to a table instead

items.title: Late dinner — Il Flauto di Pan
items.detail: In the Villa Cimbrone gardens. Rossellinis is the other option.

days.title: Up the coast to Salerno, then north by rail
days.kicker: AMALFI → FLORENCE — driver to Salerno, then Frecciarossa
days.changeNote: The old plan went Amalfi → Naples → Rome. Now Amalfi feeds straight into the Salerno–Florence Frecciarossa corridor — one long travel day instead of splitting Florence and Tuscany around it.

items.title: Check out — Anantara Convento
items.detail: Checkout is exactly noon here

items.title: Private driver to Salerno
items.detail: Along the coast road via Vietri, then a short stretch of highway — about an hour

items.title: Arrive Salerno station; lunch on the concourse
Frecciarossa to Florence
items.detail: Salerno → Firenze S.M.N., direct via Naples and Rome — about 3.5 hours. Ten-plus direct departures a day; book ahead for a better fare.

items.title: Check in — The Hoxton Florence
items.detail: Via delle Mantellate, on the quieter west side near the river

items.title: Dinner near the hotel
items.detail: Something easy after a long travel day — Borgo Ognissanti has plenty of options

days.title: All of Florence in one day
days.note: Dense by design. Everything before 1pm is ticketed and time-stamped; everything after is yours.

items.title: Accademia — David at first entry
items.detail: Forty-five minutes is genuinely enough. Go straight down the hall.

items.title: Duomo — climb Brunelleschi's dome
items.detail: 463 steps, timed slot, and much better before the day heats up

items.title: Coffee on Piazza della Signoria
items.detail: The Loggia dei Lanzi is an open-air sculpture hall and it is free

items.title: Uffizi, guided
items.detail: Botticelli, Leonardo, the Caravaggio room. Roughly two hours with a guide.

items.title: Lunch in the Oltrarno — Il Santo Bevitore
items.detail: Or Gucci Osteria if you want the splurge. Trattoria Mario is the third option if you'd rather eat near San Lorenzo.

items.title: Pitti Palace and the Boboli Gardens
items.detail: The gardens are the reason to go; climb to the top for the view back over the city

items.title: Oltrarno artisan workshops
items.detail: Via Maggio and Santo Spirito — gilders, leatherworkers, restorers still working street level

items.title: Ponte Vecchio, then up to Piazzale Michelangelo
items.detail: Sunset is around 8:00pm. Taxi up, walk down.

items.title: Dinner — Borgo San Jacopo
items.detail: Michelin-starred, on the river, with a handful of window tables. Ask for one.

days.title: Fiesole, then the quieter Florence
days.kicker: FLORENCE — hills in the morning, Santa Croce after
days.note: A lighter day after yesterday's sprint — one bus ride out of the city, then whatever's left of Florence you haven't seen yet.

items.title: Bus to Fiesole
items.detail: ATAF #7 from Piazza San Marco, about twenty minutes up into the hills

items.title: The Roman theatre and Etruscan walls
items.detail: Still-standing tiers of a 1st-century BC theatre, with the whole Arno valley behind it

items.title: Coffee on the terrace
items.detail: The view back over Florence, with Brunelleschi's dome on the skyline

items.title: Lunch — San Lorenzo Market
items.detail: The upstairs food hall, casual, no booking

items.title: San Lorenzo — the Medici Chapels
items.detail: Michelangelo's New Sacristy, a short walk from the market stalls

items.title: Santa Croce
items.detail: Michelangelo, Galileo and Machiavelli are all buried here; the Pazzi Chapel is Brunelleschi at his plainest and best

items.title: Back to the hotel to change
OPERA — La Traviata at St. Mark's Anglican
items.detail: Via Maggio, across Ponte Santa Trinita

items.title: Dinner — Trattoria Sostanza
items.detail: Cash only. The butter chicken and the tortino. Alternative: Buca dell'Orafo.

days.title: Into the Val d'Elsa, through Certaldo
days.changeNote: The rental car is picked up here, not on arrival in Florence — you don't need one for the two city days, only for Tuscany.

items.title: Check out; collect the rental car
items.detail: The agencies cluster on Borgo Ognissanti, a ten-minute walk from the Hoxton and just outside the ZTL — so you never drive into the centro storico. Have the IDP and licence ready.

items.title: Southwest out of the city
items.detail: Florence → Certaldo is about 45 minutes

items.title: Certaldo Alto, by funicular
items.detail: Boccaccio's birthplace — a walled brick town, the funicular climbs from Piazza Boccaccio in under two minutes

items.title: Casa Boccaccio
items.detail: The Decameron's author was born here; the house is now a small, quiet museum

items.title: Lunch on Via Boccaccio
items.detail: A terrace table in the upper town before the drive on

items.title: On to Castelfalfi
items.detail: About twenty-five minutes further into the Val d'Elsa

items.title: Check in — Il Castelfalfi
items.detail: A restored 14th-century hamlet on a 2,700-acre estate, its own castle at the centre

items.title: The hamlet on foot
items.detail: The piazza, the castle walls, the little church — all restored, none of it roped off

items.title: Aperitivo at Ecrù
items.detail: The estate's cocktail bar

items.title: Dinner — La Via del Sale
items.detail: The estate's fine-dining room; the vegetables and olive oil are grown on the property

days.title: Towers, then on horseback through the vines
days.kicker: TUSCANY — San Gimignano and a horseback vineyard tour
days.changeNote: Swaps the Montespertoli estate visit for a horseback tour through vineyards and olive groves near San Gimignano — it already bundles lunch and a winery, so it replaces both the old lunch stop and the afternoon wine estate in one booking.
days.note: One day for both San Gimignano and a horseback vineyard tour, now that Tuscany is down to two nights — Volterra and the separate Montespertoli visit don't fit this time.

items.title: Driver to San Gimignano
items.detail: About twenty-five minutes

items.title: The towers of San Gimignano
items.detail: Fourteen of the original seventy-two medieval towers still stand — best seen from Piazza della Cisterna

items.title: The Collegiata
items.detail: Ghirlandaio and Gozzoli frescoes wall to wall in a church the size of a chapel

items.title: Gelato at Dondoli
items.detail: A two-time world gelato champion on Piazza della Cisterna — quick, before the horses

items.title: Horseback riding, lunch and a winery
items.detail: San Gimignano Experience: about an hour in the saddle through vineyards, olive groves and native woods, then a traditional Tuscan lunch (antipasti, truffle lasagna, bread soup), a cellar tour and tastings of Chianti Classico, Vernaccia and Super Tuscans. No riding experience needed; book ahead — 3-4 hours all told.
items.how: Meet at the Bivio Volterra bus stop

items.title: Back to Castelfalfi
items.detail: About twenty-five minutes

items.title: Pool or spa terrace
items.detail: You've earned it after a day in the saddle

items.title: Dinner — La Via del Sale
items.detail: The estate's fine-dining room, on your last Tuscan night

days.title: Back to Rome, by rail
days.kicker: TUSCANY → FLORENCE → ROME — drop the car, then the train
days.changeNote: The rental car's round trip ends here — back to Florence to return it, then the Frecciarossa on to Rome.

items.title: Check out; on the road
items.detail: Back toward Florence, retracing Thursday's route

items.title: Drop off the rental car
items.detail: Borgo Ognissanti — reservation #21586310US4 ends here

items.title: Frecciarossa to Rome
items.detail: Firenze S.M.N. → Roma Termini, direct — about 1.5 hours

items.title: Arrive Roma Termini; taxi to the hotel
Check in — Nobu Hotel Roma
items.detail: Via Vittorio Veneto, at the top of the street by Villa Borghese — five minutes from Wednesday's photo spot

items.title: Last Roman afternoon — Via Veneto and the Spanish Steps
items.detail: La Dolce Vita's old strip, then down to Piazza di Spagna

items.title: Farewell dinner — Nobu Roma
items.detail: The hotel's namesake restaurant, for the last night

items.title: Taxi to FCO
items.detail: About forty minutes on an empty Sunday road. No rental to return this time — that ended in Florence on Sep 5.

items.title: Check in and bag drop
items.detail: Three hours ahead for an intercontinental departure

items.title: FCO → IAH
items.detail: Arrivederci, Italia.

driversNote: Almost the whole trip is car-free: a private driver in from FCO, the Frecciarossa to Naples, ferries to Capri and on to Amalfi, a private driver over to Ravello and later to Salerno, and the Frecciarossa up to Florence. The rental is only collected on Sep 3, on Borgo Ognissanti just outside Florence's ZTL, and returned to the same spot on Sep 5 before the train to Rome — two driving days, not fourteen. The IDP ships by Aug 3; pack it with the physical licence even though it's only needed that once. Never drive into the historic centre — Florence's ZTL alone is ~€200 a crossing. Castelfalfi has its own parking. The Naples–Positano–Amalfi ferry only runs July–August, so there's no fallback date if it's ever cancelled for weather — have the hotel's driver number ready as backup.

bookings.item: Book the FCO → Hotel Trame private driver
bookings.detail: Pre-booked NCC, meeting you inside arrivals with a name board — roughly €70–90 for the two of you, against a €55 flat-rate official taxi if you would rather just walk to the rank. Give them the ITA flight number so the driver tracks the landing.

bookings.item: Frecciarossa tickets — Roma Termini → Napoli Centrale, Aug 27
bookings.detail: Runs roughly every half hour, about 1h10 — book ahead for the fare, not because it sells out.

bookings.item: Naples → Amalfi ferry via Positano, Aug 29
bookings.detail: Positano Jet's seasonal route, July–August only. Book the Amalfi-bound leg specifically, and check the current 2026 timetable close to the date — schedules shift with the season.

bookings.item: Rebook the rental car — Florence pickup and drop-off, Sep 3 → Sep 5
bookings.detail: Reservation #21586310US4 is still FCO Aug 24 → FCO Sep 6. It needs to become Borgo Ognissanti, Florence, Sep 3 → Florence Sep 5: two days rather than fourteen, both ends the same city. A different pickup/drop-off city usually carries a fee, so the €1,087.81 quote will not hold — re-quote before cancelling.
Grand Hotel Vesuvio's Michelin-starred rooftop room only takes reservations up to 14 days out — put a reminder in your calendar rather than trying to book now.

bookings.item: Capri ferry — Naples → Capri return, Aug 28
bookings.detail: Fast ferries from Molo Beverello take about fifty minutes; NLG, SNAV and Caremar all run the route. Book both legs online the night before rather than queueing at the counter, and note the last sailing back. The round-the-island boat can be picked up at Marina Grande on the day.
Direct via Naples and Rome, about 3.5 hours, 10+ departures a day — book ahead for a better fare, not out of scarcity.
About 1.5 hours, frequent departures — no need to lock this in until closer to the date.

bookings.item: Vatican early entry (Aug 25), Colosseum arena floor (Aug 26)
bookings.detail: Both need booking — the Vatican slots go first.

bookings.item: Timed entries — Accademia, Duomo dome, Uffizi, all on Sep 1
bookings.detail: Three in one morning, in that order. Book the dome climb first; it has the fewest slots.

bookings.item: Florence opera — La Traviata at St. Mark's, Sep 2
bookings.detail: Now on the second, lighter Florence day rather than the arrival evening — book before the seats go.

bookings.item: Rome opera — All Saints' Anglican, Aug 25
bookings.detail: Confirm the programme is posted before booking.

bookings.item: Horseback riding, lunch & winery tour — San Gimignano, Fri Sep 4
bookings.detail: San Gimignano Experience, 11am–3pm, ~€120pp: about an hour on horseback through vineyards and olive groves, then lunch, a cellar tour and wine tastings. Replaces the old Montespertoli visit. Meets at the Bivio Volterra bus stop — book ahead, it's a small-group tour.

bookings.item: Reserve dinners at Il Castelfalfi — La Via del Sale, Sep 3 & 4
bookings.detail: The estate's fine-dining room. Worth booking ahead even though the room itself is already confirmed.

bookings.item: Ravello Festival — check the Aug 30 programme
bookings.detail: Festival runs to Sep 5, so your one Ravello night is well inside the window.
The hotel's own restaurant, on your last night — worth reserving ahead given the brand.

Caruso Roof Garden Aug 27 · Palazzo Petrucci Aug 28 · Dei Cappuccini Aug 29 · Borgo San Jacopo Sep 1 · Sostanza Sep 2 · La Via del Sale Sep 3 & 4. Plus Armando, Roscioli, Da Enzo, Lo Scoglio — reserve ahead where they take bookings.

bookingsRuledOut.reason: No open night in the schedule for a Verona detour — every night from Aug 24 to Sep 5 has a confirmed hotel booking elsewhere.
Fit fine as a full day when Tuscany was three nights; with the coast now taking a night from it, San Gimignano and the horseback vineyard tour fill the single Tuscan day instead.

budget.note: 6 hotels, 13 nights — all six are now confirmed bookings. Trame ($1,588), Grand Hotel Vesuvio ($1,180), Anantara Convento ($4,115.74, includes breakfast for two and a $100 experience credit), The Hoxton ($1,492), Castelfalfi ($2,848), Nobu Hotel Roma ($874).

Estimate. FCO private driver, Rome→Naples train, Naples↔Capri ferry, Naples→Amalfi→Positano ferry, Amalfi→Salerno private driver, Salerno→Florence train, a 2-day Florence–Tuscany rental car, and Florence→Rome train.
Vatican, Colosseum, Capri boat tour, Florence galleries, operas, and the San Gimignano horseback/lunch/winery tour (~€120pp, ~$260 for two) — no Pompeii or Volterra guide fees this time.
Taxis, tips, Naples street food, incidentals.

photographers.spots: Pincio terrace and Villa Borghese at sunset; the Colosseum and Trevi at dawn, empty; the Spanish Steps
Positano's pastel stairs, seen from the ferry; the Ravello gardens; Amalfi's Duomo steps
Piazzale Michelangelo at sunset; Ponte Vecchio at dawn; the Fiesole hillside; the Uffizi loggia
San Gimignano's towers at golden hour; the Castelfalfi vineyards and golf course; on horseback in the vines outside town
Gardens of Augustus over the Faraglioni; Via Krupp; Marina Grande

photographersNote: Trip.com has no reliable Italy 旅拍 listings. Book through Flytographer or Localgrapher and request a Mandarin-speaking photographer in the notes, or find 旅拍 photographers directly on 小红书 using the searches above. Shoot dawn for empty landmarks, golden hour for the coast and the Tuscan hills.
